items.title: Longtime GTA Fan Passes Away Weeks Before GTA 6 Release, Community Pays Tribute
points: Jerry Fort, the terminally ill GTA 6 fan who wanted to stream the game after its November 19, 2026, release, has sadly passed away following a severe infection and health complications after his transplant surgery.
Fort’s sister uploaded a TikTok video on November 2, via his social channels (VoidOnly), confirming that he passed away on October 29.
She also expressed her gratitude to the GTA community, which raised $50,000 to help Jerry make it to the game’s release, and shared how much she had hoped he would live to see that day.

Back in August 2026, Jerry Fort shared a TikTok video explaining that his lungs had attached to his chest wall, making the transplant extremely dangerous because doctors would need to separate and remove them before replacing them.
However, shortly before GTA 6’s Extended Look premiered in late August, the gaming community helped push his GoFundMe donations past their original goal, giving Jerry renewed hope.

Gubenthiran (48), the lorry driver from Vaniyambadi town, and Mohammed Rafiq (39), lorry cleaner from Vaniyambadi town.

India’s tax hike drives illegal gold imports to 3-year high
points: India’s illegal gold imports surged to the highest since 2023 in the third quarter as a government duty hike spurred use of unofficial channels, according to a report from the World Gold Council.
Informal shipments for July to September jumped more than 1,500 per cent to 50 metric tons from 3 tons a year earlier, the producer-funded group said, citing data from consultancy Metals Focus.
The report gave no details on how the trade is tracked.
Such imports typically go through avenues that avoid official duties, like smuggling or small quantities brought in by individuals.
The informal bullion market in the world’s second-largest consumer has flourished since the government more than doubled import levies on gold and silver to 15 per cent earlier this year.
The move was as part of efforts to curb purchases as India tackles a ballooning trade deficit due to higher energy prices.

items.title: Technical snag suspected after 2 helicopters collide near Everest Base Camp
points: A technical glitch may have led to the collision between two helicopters as they were about to land at a high-altitude Himalayan helipad at Pheriche in Nepal’s Solukhumbu on Tuesday, a Nepalese official said, ruling out weather as a cause.
A tourist from Chennai, Vasanth Kumar Balaramaramadu, 47, died on the spot, and three others were injured in the collision.
While details of how the crash took place will be known after investigation, it appears there was some technical glitch,” Solukhumbu’s chief development officer Kaman Singh Thapa Magar told HT.

He added that a Fishtail Air helicopter carrying two passengers from Gorakhshep (about 5164 m above sea level, near Everest Base Camp at 5364 m) collided with another Air Dynasty chopper carrying cargo at Pheriche (4371 m) at 8:11am (7:56am IST).
He added that the two injured are under treatment in Kathmandu and Balaramaramadu’s body is at Lukla, the closest airstrip to the Everest Base Camp region.

items.title: Centre proposes 10 new import gateways for drugs, medical devices
points: The proposed amendment to Rule 43A of the Drugs Rules, 1945, is aimed at easing import operations, reducing inland transportation distances and improving the movement of healthcare products across the country.

The additional locations proposed include ICD Sonipat, Piyala and Harsaru in Haryana; ICD Dadri in Uttar Pradesh; ICD Gandhidham/Mundra in Gujarat; ICD Sanath Nagar and Thimmapur in Hyderabad, Telangana; and ICD Whitefield in Bengaluru, Karnataka.
The Ministry has also proposed including SEZ Bommasandra in Karnataka and Noida International Airport in Uttar Pradesh for the import of drugs by air.

The proposed additions will supplement the existing network of authorised import gateways, which includes ICDs at Dhannad and Tihi in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, besides airports already notified for drug imports.
Rule 43A specifies the ports, airports, railway stations, road crossings and other entry points through which drugs can be imported into India.
According to the Ministry, expanding the network is expected to allow importers to clear consignments closer to their manufacturing facilities, warehouses and distribution centres.

The system, which had a windspeed of 110 kmph to 120 kmph during the landfall time, may weaken gradually into a cyclonic storm and wind speed may also slightly come down to 80-90 kmph, gusting to 100 kmph, by noon.

J Appalakonda, mother of J Vamsi, said her son went to Russia expecting employment but found no work after reaching there, and that he subsequently got in touch with a Nepali national who promised him better-paying employment in Ukraine and took him there.
